The 2 Hebrew quotes collate at byte tier against the refs they are cited to (collate.py: oshb:Ps.87.1 byte, oshb:Ps.87.3 byte), and their English is WEB text as rendered — “His foundation is in the holy mountains.” (web:Ps.87.1) and “Glorious things are spoken about you, city of God. Selah.” (web:Ps.87.3). The selah citation is exact against the inventory (pmarks_Ps.json selah: Ps.87.3 = 1 occurrence, single-witness) and functions as corroboration, not as the seam driver; the driver is the 1cs speech onset at oshb:Ps.87.4 = web:Ps.87.4, a tier-1 discourse frame, so the 87:3|87:4 seam holds, the medium confidence is calibrated for a 3-verse strophe in a 7-verse psalm, and I contest neither the span nor the unit_type nor the rejected_alternative. challenges.claim: observed_substrate_signals[0] misstates oshb:Ps.87.1 in 2 ways: the opening clause does have an expressed subject noun of its own, and the title colon holds no city that the clause could carry over as its referent.
challenges.evidence: Spliced from verse_map_oshb.json and collated with collate.py (byte tier at oshb:Ps.87.1 for both runs): MT 87:1's title colon is לִבְנֵי קֹ֭רַח מִזְמ֣וֹר שִׁ֑יר — 4 tokens, no city noun — and the clause after it opens on יְ֝סוּדָת֗וֹ, which is itself the verbless clause's expressed subject noun (the row quotes that same token at byte tier). Sweeps place the city elsewhere: skeleton עיר occurs in 1 verse of Psalm 87 (oshb:Ps.87.3 = web:Ps.87.3; 25 verses book-wide) and skeleton ציון in 2 verses of Psalm 87 (oshb:Ps.87.2 and oshb:Ps.87.5; 38 verses book-wide), 0 of them in the title colon. Grammar blocks the proposed referent independently: this psalm's city is feminine in 2 verses — מְדֻבָּ֣ר בָּ֑ךְ at oshb:Ps.87.3, יֻלַּד בָּ֑הּ and וְה֖וּא יְכוֹנְנֶ֣הָ עֶלְיֽוֹן at oshb:Ps.87.5 — which both witnesses show, “Glorious things are spoken about you, city of God.” (web:Ps.87.3) and “the Most High himself will establish her.” (web:Ps.87.5), so the masculine suffix on יְ֝סוּדָת֗וֹ cannot take the city as antecedent. Psalm 87 is an identity psalm under the offset map, so the oshb and web refs cited here pair one to one across all 7 verses.

The runs diverge in 2 places: the demonstrative carries U+059D plus U+0597 at 87:4 against U+0596 at 87:6, and the closing token carries U+05BD at 87:4 against U+05A3 at 87:6. Since accent_stripped is limited to U+0591-U+05AF, that U+05BD survives stripping and the 2 runs stay unequal at accent_stripped tier; skeleton is the first tier that collapses them, and skeleton זה ילד שם hits 2 verses book-wide. The repetition is real and the row's count of 2 verses is correct — the repair is the tier label, in the rationale and in observed_substrate_signals[0] together, since both state the byte claim.

reviews.reasoning: No claim in this row failed re-derivation, so I support it. Psalm 88 is shift+1 with mt_title_verses [1], so the row's ladder from web:Ps.88.0 = oshb:Ps.88.1 through web:Ps.88.7 = oshb:Ps.88.8 is arithmetically exact, title pseudo-ref included. The 8 labels reproduce psalm_device_inventory.json's superscriptions entry for 88 item for item (mizmor, shir, maskil, lamnatseach, livnei_qorach, le_heman, al_machalat, leannot), and the 8th of those, le_heman, is the label carried by the row's byte-tier quote; genre_label_membership le_heman = [88], so the cited figure of 1 psalm is right. I tested the exclusivity claim independently by reading all 11 livnei_qorach titles (42, 44, 45, 46, 47, 48, 49, 84, 85, 87, 88): 1 of those 11 names an individual, “A contemplation by Heman, the Ezrahite.” (web:Ps.88.0). Both Hebrew quotes collate at byte tier against their cited refs, the invocation gloss “Yahweh, the God of my salvation” (web:Ps.88.1) is WEB text as rendered, and the rear-seam selah is exact (pmarks_Ps.json selah: Ps.88.8 = 1 occurrence, single-witness = web:Ps.88.7). That rear seam does not rest on selah alone: oshb:Ps.88.9 = web:Ps.88.8 opens the psalm's envelope, which I document in my challenge on the next span and which is an independent tier-1 reason to break after web:Ps.88.7, so high confidence is calibrated. Two observations that do not rise to defects: observed_substrate_signals[2] calls web:Ps.88.1-Ps.88.7 one continuous 2nd-person address, and 2 of those 7 verses carry no 2nd-person form at all (oshb:Ps.88.4 and oshb:Ps.88.5 = web:Ps.88.3 and web:Ps.88.4), so the vocative frame is unbroken but the morphology is not; and device_notes reproduces the rationale's opening sentence word for word.

The span itself is defensible and I do not contest it: the front seam is the selah-marked close at web:Ps.88.7 = oshb:Ps.88.8 plus the turn to social isolation, the rear seam at web:Ps.88.12|web:Ps.88.13 is the fronted 1cs pronoun opening oshb:Ps.88.14, the row's 1 Hebrew quote collates at byte tier against oshb:Ps.88.11, the 2 selah citations are exact (pmarks_Ps.json: Ps.88.8 and Ps.88.11, 1 occurrence each, single-witness), and the shift+1 arithmetic is right in all 6 refs. Three evidence defects stand: the rear-seam verse the row argues from is missing from boundary_evidence_refs; a byte-true structural device spanning the psalm straddles this row's rear seam undisclosed; and the interrogative count names no unit and undercounts what both witnesses carry.

reviews.reasoning: This row verifies broadly. The front seam is real: oshb:Ps.88.14 = web:Ps.88.13 opens on the fronted 1cs pronoun the row quotes, that quote collates at byte tier, and so does the psalm's closing token at oshb:Ps.88.19 = web:Ps.88.18. The absence claim is correct and correctly span-scoped: pmarks_Ps.json records selah in Psalm 88 at Ps.88.8 and Ps.88.11, that is 2 verses, giving 0 inside oshb:Ps.88.14-Ps.88.19 = web:Ps.88.13-Ps.88.18, and I read all 6 verses in both witnesses for a praise or resolution clause and found 0. The shift+1 arithmetic is exact in all 8 refs, and the out-of-span range the prose argues (web:Ps.88.10-Ps.88.12) is mirrored in boundary_evidence_refs. I also note, without filing it, that the 1-word gloss in curly quotes near the end of the rationale is not WEB wording (WEB closes that verse with a period, not a comma) — check_web_quotes skips spans under 2 words, so the convention does not reach it. The filed defect is that the row builds an affirmative closural argument on the psalm's closing verse while quoting, undisclosed, 1 half of a byte-true envelope whose other half sits outside the span.
